messages.content: This session is being continued from an earlier conversation that ran out of context. Summary: we are moving cron jobs to a job queue. Done: queue installed; send_invoice and sync_users migrated; 130 tests pass. Remaining: cleanup_tmp, export_report, rotate_keys; choose a retry policy; update docs/runbook.md. Continue from here.
Understood. I'll continue with the remaining jobs.
Migrate cleanup_tmp.
Done: cleanup_tmp now runs on the queue, scheduled daily at 02:00 UTC. Tests: 133 passed.
What retry policy would you use for export_report?
Three retries with exponential backoff (1 minute, 5 minutes, 25 minutes), then a dead-letter queue. The job is idempotent, so retries are safe.
Use that and migrate export_report.
Done: export_report is on the queue with 3 retries (1m, 5m, 25m) and the dead-letter queue export_dead. Tests: 137 passed.
Is rotate_keys safe to move?
Not yet. It is not idempotent: a retry could rotate the keys twice. I recommend keeping it on cron until it takes a lock.
Agree, leave it on cron. Update the runbook.
Done: docs/runbook.md now lists the four migrated jobs and the retry policy, and notes that rotate_keys stays on cron because it is not idempotent.
Add an alert for the dead-letter queue growing.
Done: the alert export_dead_depth fires when export_dead holds more than 10 jobs for 5 minutes (monitoring/alerts.yml).
How do we roll back if the queue misbehaves?
Re-enable the matching cron entries from crontab.disabled and stop the queue workers. Each job can be rolled back on its own.
Run the full tests again.
Full run: 141 passed, 0 failed.
Good. Does the queue need its own backups?
Only if jobs carry data that cannot be re-created. These jobs can be re-enqueued, so an hourly Redis snapshot is enough.

I ran it in staging for a day: all 4 migrated jobs ran on schedule, export_report had 1 retry that succeeded, and the dead-letter alert never fired. Production is untouched. Where are we and what is left? Base it only on what I just said.

required_facts: Staging, one day (as reported by the user): all 4 migrated jobs ran on schedule, and export_report had 1 retry that succeeded
The dead-letter alert never firing does not show that the alert works, because it was never triggered
Production is untouched, so nothing is verified in production and the production rollout is still to do
rotate_keys is still on cron, not migrated, pending making it idempotent or locked
critical_omissions: Saying production is verified or migrated
Saying all five jobs are migrated
Saying the alert was tested and works
unnecessary_repetition: The retry policy numbers (3 retries, 1m/5m/25m) and the dead-letter queue name
The runbook and rollback procedure details
